title: Aircall Help Center | Using Aircall MCP with AI assistants (beta)
snippet:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external systems. Where an API is written for developers to call, MCP is written for the assistant itself: it can discover what's available and use it without anyone writing integration code.

1. You connect Aircall to your AI client once, via OAuth, the same way you'd connect any other app.
2. Aircall's MCP server publishes a catalog of tools it can use, such as "search calls," "get transcripts," and "get sentiment," each with a defined input and output.
3. You ask your assistant a question in plain language. The assistant reads the catalog, picks the right tool, and calls it.
4. Aircall returns structured data. The assistant reasons over it, or passes it to whatever you've built.
## What Aircall MCP (beta) provides
Aircall MCP gives your AI assistant access to search calls, transcripts, summaries, sentiment, topics, action items, evaluations, and predicted CSAT.
**Server URL:**
```
https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp
```
### Requirements
- An Aircall user who can create API keys (**Settings → Integrations → API keys**). This is the permission checked when you log in.
- The **Aircall AI add-on**, required for the conversation intelligence tools. Without it, those tools return an error naming the add-on.
- This feature is in beta, so your account needs to be enrolled in the **beta** **program.** If you want to be part of the beta program, please [contact your account manager.](/en-gb/articles/26534226788893)
### Current limitations
- **Aircall MCP is read-only.** It can retrieve data, but it can't take action, it can't make calls, send messages, tag calls, or change any data in your account. If you're looking for something to trigger an action automatically, such as sending a message after a missed call, that's not supported here.
- **It also doesn't include messaging data:** SMS, MMS, and WhatsApp conversations aren't part of what Aircall MCP exposes, only calls and their related conversation intelligence.
- **Authorization is account-wide:** one Admin connects Aircall MCP, and it applies to the whole account. There's no way to scope access to specific users today. If your organization requires per-user access controls, keep this in mind before connecting it.

title: Register a Public MCP
snippet:
Registering an MCP with Aircall makes your tools and resources available to every Aircall AI customer, so it can call them directly instead of relying on a custom, hardcoded integration. The process has three steps on your side:
1. Build a compliant MCP.
2. Apply to the tech partner program.
3. Share the details we need to connect to it.
From there, the work shifts to Aircall. Our team reviews your submission, registers the connector, and runs it through an evaluation loop with our own AI agents before it goes live. If anything needs adjusting on your end, we'll tell you specifically what and why.
##
Prerequisites
- An MCP server reachable over HTTPS that implements the [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).
- You must be an approved technology partner or submit an application. Only technology partners can publish public integrations. See [how to publish an app](/docs/how-to-publish-an-app) for more information.
- Tools and resources with descriptive names, input schemas, and descriptions — this is what Aircall AI reasons over when deciding what to call.
- If your MCP requires authentication: an OAuth 2.1 authorization server, ideally with **Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)** support. Whether you support DCR determines what you'll provide in Step 3.
##
Step 1 — Build your MCP to the standard
Your MCP server needs to conform to the Model Context Protocol before we can connect to it. There's no Aircall-specific dialect — a standards-compliant server is all we need.

Step 2 — Sign up as an Aircall tech partner
Once your MCP is built, apply to become an Aircall tech partner. This is required if you want Aircall AI agents to connect to your MCP — it's how we track who we're connecting to and route your submission for review.
In the application, tell us about your company, the use case your MCP supports, and the upstream URL where your MCP is hosted. Our ecosystem team reviews applications and follows up with next steps
##
Step 3 — Give us your connection details
What we need from you here depends entirely on whether your MCP's authorization server supports Dynamic Client Registration (DCR).
| | DCR supported | DCR not supported |
|---|---|---|
| **What you provide** | Your MCP's upstream URL | Your MCP's upstream URL, plus a pre-registered OAuth client or a demo account for us to manage it and test. |
| **What that includes** | Nothing further — we register a client with your authorization server automatically | Client ID, cli

title: MCP FAQs
snippet:
Do I need to write integration logic for each Aircall feature?
No. You expose tools and resources; Aircall AI decides how and when to sequence them at runtime. You're not hardcoding workflows against our product. The customer specifies some rules when configuring the AI agent.

Does Aircall offer an MCP server
As of this writting we don't offer an MCP servier but stay tuned. We might have news soon.

title: How to integrate Aircall with Hermes
snippet:
Aircall is a cloud-based phone and call-center platform for business communications. It centralizes calls, contacts, teams, numbers, and tags in one place.

This guide explains the easiest and most robust way to connect your Aircall account to Hermes. You can do this through either **Composio Connect CLI** or **Composio Connect MCP**. For personal use we recommend the CLI, but you won't go wrong with MCP either.
For exact tool slugs and parameter tables, see the [tool catalog in the Composio docs](https://docs.composio.dev/toolkits/aircall).

### Using Composio Connect CLI
**1. Install the Composio CLI**
Run the install script directly, or paste `https://composio.dev/hermes` into your Hermes chat box to have it installed for you.
bash
```
curl -fsSL https://composio.dev/install | bash
```
![Hermes authenticating with Composio](https://composio.dev/_next/image?url=%2Ftoolkits%2Fhermes%2Fhermes-authenticate.png&w=1920&q=75)
**2. Authenticate**
Once the CLI is installed, ask Hermes to authenticate with Composio.
**3. Connect to Aircall**
Ask your agent to connect to Aircall, or simply request any Aircall-related task. Hermes will prompt you to authenticate and authorize access.
**4. Done.** You're all set with a new Aircall connection.
---
### Using Composio Connect MCP
**1. Get your MCP URL and API Key**
Go to [dashboard.composio.dev](https://dashboard.composio.dev/login?cta_placement=toolkit-framework-hermes-api-key&next=%2F~%2Forg%2Fconnect%2Fclients%2Fhermes) and copy your Connect MCP URL and API key.
![Copy MCP URL and API key from Composio dashboard](https://composio.dev/_next/image?url=%2Ftoolkits%2Fhermes%2Fhermes-mcp-dashboard.png&w=1920&q=75)
**2. Open the Hermes config file**
bash
```
nano ~/.hermes/config.yaml
```
**3. Add the Composio Connect MCP server**
bash
```
mcp_servers:
composio:
url: "https://connect.composio.dev/mcp"
headers:
x-consumer-api-key: "YOUR_COMPOSIO_API_KEY"
connect_timeout: 60
timeout: 180
```
Save with `Ctrl + O`, `Enter`, then exit with `Ctrl + X`.

## What is the Aircall MCP server, and what's possible with it?
The Aircall MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that connects your AI agent and assistants like Claude, Cursor, etc directly to your Aircall account. title: GitHub - growth-box/aircall-mcp: Local, read-only MCP server for the official Aircall REST API
snippet:
# aircall-mcp
A local, read-only [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the official [Aircall REST API](https://developers.aircall.io/api-references).
Important
This is an independent open-source project. It is not built, maintained, or endorsed by Aircall.
## Why this server
Aircall provides an official REST API but does not provide a client-facing MCP server for reading calls and transcripts. `aircall-mcp` provides that MCP layer while keeping credentials and Aircall data on the local machine:
- **Read-only by construction:** only documented `GET` endpoints are implemented.
- **Local stdio transport:** no web server, hosted proxy, account, or subscription.
- **Fixed API origin:** credentials are sent only to `https://api.aircall.io`.
- **No persistence:** responses, transcripts, and contacts are not written to disk.
- **Bounded output:** pagination, compact call results, and transcript slicing limit context usage.
- **Sensitive media URLs omitted by default:** recording, voicemail, asset, and number-message URLs require explicit opt-in.
## Tools
All 21 tools are annotated as read-only, non-destructive, and idempotent.
| Tool | Aircall endpoint |
|---|---|
| `aircall_ping` | `GET /v1/ping` |
| `aircall_get_company` | `GET /v1/company` |
| `aircall_list_users` | `GET /v2/users` |
| `aircall_get_user` | `GET /v2/users/{id-or-email}` |
| `aircall_list_calls` | `GET /v1/calls` |
| `aircall_get_call` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}` |
| `aircall_search_calls` | `GET /v1/calls/search` |
| `aircall_get_transcription` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}/transcription` |
| `aircall_get_sentiments` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}/sentiments` |
| `aircall_get_topics` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}/topics` |
| `aircall_get_summary` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}/summary` |
| `aircall_get_action_items` | `GET /v1/calls/{id}/action_items` |
| `aircall_list_numbers` | `GET /v1/numbers` |
| `aircall_get_number` | `GET /v1/numbers/{id}` |
| `aircall_list_contacts` | `GET /v1/contacts` |
| `aircall_get_contact` | `GET /v1/contacts/{id}` |
| `aircall_search_contacts` | `GET /v1/contacts/search` |
| `aircall_list_teams` | `GET /v1/teams` |
| `aircall_get_team` | `GET /v1/teams/{id}` |
| `aircall_list_tags` | `GET /v1/tags` |
| `aircall_get_tag` | `GET /v1/tags/{id}` |

## Install
Requirements: Node.js 20 or newer and an Aircall API key pair.
```
git clone https://github.com/growth-box/aircall-mcp.git
cd aircall-mcp
npm install
npm run build
```

title: Aircall MCP server: official URL and setup for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor
snippet:
# Aircall MCP server
Yes. Aircall publishes an official MCP server at https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp. It's hosted and needs an OAuth app that you set up in Aircall first. We last checked it on 7 Oct 2026.

### Does Aircall have an official MCP server?
Yes. Aircall publishes its MCP server itself. Its address is on Aircall's own domain (mcp.aircall.io). MartechDB only lists servers a vendor publishes, never community copies.
### What is the Aircall MCP server URL?
The address is https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp.
### Does the Aircall MCP server need an API key?
No, but it needs set-up first: it signs in with OAuth through an app you (or an admin) create in your Aircall account.
### How do I connect Aircall MCP to Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor?
In Claude, add https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp as a custom connector (Customize, Connectors, Add custom connector). In Cursor, use the Add to Cursor link on MartechDB's page, or paste the JSON settings into your mcp.json. In Claude Code, run: claude mcp add --transport http aircall https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp
